**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at that price for about $9,801 — comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap, well under the $20,000 daily limit, and requiring no fund transfers. The case for buying rests on Apple's operating performance: **operating income rose to $123,216 million in fiscal 2024 from $114,301 million**, a 7.8% increase, on total net sales of $391,035 million (+2%), with Services growing 13% to $96,169 million and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%, while cash generated by operating activities was a robust $118,254 million. I noted that net income fell to $93,736 million from $96,995 million, but this was driven entirely by a non-operating, one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge tied to the European Commission's State Aid Decision — pre-tax income actually improved to $123,485 million — so the underlying operating trajectory is positive. The limit price was set at the current market (last $222.70, ask $222.72, bid $222.68 as of 15:05 UTC on 2024-11-06) to satisfy the "close to market price" requirement, and the order remains within the AAPL/MSFT, buy-only mandate.
